newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Firmer with 180-cst deal at $100/T.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Firmer with 180-cst deal at $100/T.

text.p: Continued buying interest from a local trader supported the Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market on Thursday and traders said sentiment was likely to stay firm in the near term.
Late on Thursday, a deal for the 180-cst grade was done at $100.00 per tonne fob for August 5-9 lifting, traders said.
The 180-cst grade was last traded on Monday at $99.00 with two cargoes exchanging hands.
A local trader and its sister company have bought more than ten 20,000-tonne cargoes since late June. The trader said the purchases were to cover its short-position on term contracts.
"Buying is likely to continue but I don't think trade will be volatile," said one trader, noting a lack of additional demand other than the local trader.
On the supply side, Sri Lanka's state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC) has issued a tender to sell 18,000-20,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil.
The tender, which offers the 3.5-percent fuel oil for lifting July 22-23, will close on July 15.
Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) will also close a tender on July 15 to sell 30,000 tonnes of 3.0-percent sulphur 180-cst fuel oil for August 1-5 lifting.
Also on Thursday, Taiwan's CPC said it had sold two 38,000-tonne fuel oil cargoes at $132.00 and $123.00 per tonne for August 16-30 delivery.

The first 0.5-percent cargo was sold at around $132.00 and the second 1.0-percent cargo, with an American Petroleum Institute (API) gravity of 15 degrees and a viscosity of 140-centistoke, was sold at about $123 per tonne.
On SIMEX fuel oil futures contract, August contract was traded at $99.00 per tonne with 20 100-tonne lots traded.
Fuel oil swaps also firmed over support from the physical market, with July traded up to $99.25/$100.25 from Wednesday's $98.50/$99.25.
